assertion.rationale: F1: data-api's middleware chain has a readOnlyGuard but no authentication layer in front of it, so external ingress meant any caller could execute any exposed transaction (feed reads, table scans) without being limited to a permitted set. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so data-api's transactions are reachable only through the server-side nginx proxy inside the Container Apps environment — both frontends' nginx.conf.template already carried the /api/ proxy rule, verified present in both, so this closes the gap without adding a token to distribute or rotate. F13: zero workload RBAC exists in IaC — there is no principal-scoped restriction on which transactions or functions each workload identity may perform; the only grants that exist are subscription-scoped Owner (deployer) and Reader (verifier), an all-or-nothing shape with no per-function limitation for data-api, mcp-tools or cost-ingest. F13 is NOT closed; it is Task 12, pending. Overall status stays GAP: F1 is closed, but F13's absent workload RBAC means transactions still are not limited to authorized processes by construction, independent of network reachability.

recommendation: Express the seven documented workload RBAC grants in IaC scoped to the specific transactions each principal needs (SQL contained-database user, Fabric Viewer, Log Analytics Reader, Security Reader, Cost Management Reader, Storage Blob Data Contributor/Reader) rather than the current all-or-nothing subscription grants. (Setting ingressExternal:false on data-api, recommended here previously, is DONE — Task 6.)
